prompt: Which of the following best defines crowding out?

options.label: A
options.text: Increased government borrowing shifts the supply of loanable funds right and increases private investment

options.label: B
options.text: Reduced government borrowing shifts the demand for loanable funds right and decreases private investment

options.label: C
options.text: Increased government borrowing raises the real interest rate and reduces interest-sensitive private-sector spending

options.label: D
options.text: Reduced government borrowing raises the real interest rate and reduces interest-sensitive private-sector spending

options.label: E
options.text: Increased government borrowing lowers the real interest rate and increases interest-sensitive private-sector spending

explanation: Crowding out is the adverse effect of additional government borrowing on interest-sensitive private spending. The borrowing pressure raises the equilibrium real interest rate, making some private borrowing and investment less attractive.

prompt: When a government runs a budget deficit, it typically finances the shortfall by

options.label: A
options.text: Lowering the equilibrium real interest rate

options.label: B
options.text: Increasing the supply of private saving

options.label: C
options.text: Borrowing funds from financial markets

options.label: D
options.text: Reducing the demand for loanable funds

options.label: E
options.text: Increasing private investment spending

explanation: A budget deficit means current revenues are insufficient to cover current outlays. The government therefore typically borrows to finance the shortfall, creating the starting point for the crowding-out mechanism.

prompt: If government borrowing increases, which of the following will most likely occur in the loanable funds market, other things equal?

options.label: A
options.text: There will be only a movement along the existing demand curve

options.label: B
options.text: The demand for loanable funds will shift to the right

options.label: C
options.text: The demand for loanable funds will shift to the left

options.label: D
options.text: The supply of loanable funds will shift to the left

options.label: E
options.text: The supply of loanable funds will shift to the right

explanation: Government borrowing is part of the demand for loanable funds.

prompt: If the demand for loanable funds increases while supply is unchanged, the equilibrium real interest rate will most likely

options.label: A
options.text: Remain unchanged

options.label: B
options.text: Decrease

options.label: C
options.text: Become unrelated to private borrowing

options.label: D
options.text: Increase

options.label: E
options.text: Fall to zero

explanation: A rightward shift of loanable-funds demand creates excess demand at the original real interest rate.

prompt: A higher equilibrium real interest rate caused by government borrowing will most likely cause private investment to

options.label: A
options.text: Increase because government borrowing supplies more funds to private firms

options.label: B
options.text: Decrease because fewer investment projects remain profitable to finance

options.label: C
options.text: Remain unchanged because private investment is independent of financing costs

options.label: D
options.text: Increase because a higher borrowing cost raises expected project profitability

options.label: E
options.text: Decrease only because the supply of loanable funds must shift left

explanation: A higher real interest rate raises the cost of financing investment projects. Some projects that were worthwhile at the lower rate are no longer profitable, so private investment decreases.

prompt: The private-sector spending reduced by crowding out is described in the CED as

options.label: A
options.text: Government purchases financed by current tax revenue

options.label: B
options.text: All private-sector spending regardless of financing conditions

options.label: C
options.text: Private saving that does not respond to interest rates

options.label: D
options.text: Interest-sensitive private-sector spending

options.label: E
options.text: Only private consumption paid for with current income

explanation: Crowding out operates through the real interest rate, so the spending most directly affected is spending that responds to borrowing costs. Private investment is the central AP example of such interest-sensitive spending.

options.label: E
options.text: Budget surplus → government borrowing increases → real interest rate rises → private investment decreases

prompt: The government cuts taxes without reducing spending and finances the larger deficit by borrowing. Which effect is most consistent with crowding out?

options.label: E
options.text: Demand for loanable funds shifts right, placing upward pressure on the real interest rate

explanation: What matters for the crowding-out channel is the increase in government borrowing, not whether the deficit arose from higher purchases or lower taxes. More borrowing shifts loanable-funds demand right and tends to raise the real interest rate.

prompt: Compared with borrowing-financed spending, government spending financed fully by an equal increase in current tax revenue will most directly

options.label: A

options.label: B

options.label: E
options.text: Cause greater crowding out because the government collects more current revenue

explanation: Crowding out in Topic 5.5 is tied to increased government borrowing. If current taxes fully finance the additional spending, the government does not need the same increase in borrowing, so the direct crowding-out pressure is smaller.

options.label: A

options.label: C

options.label: D
options.text: Necessarily eliminate all private investment spending

options.label: E
options.text: Raise private investment by the same amount as government borrowing

explanation: Crowding out is an offsetting effect: the fiscal action may increase demand directly while higher real interest rates reduce some private spending. It does not imply that the entire fiscal expansion is reversed or that all private investment disappears.

prompt: Which statement correctly distinguishes the short-run and potential long-run effects of crowding out?

options.text: Private interest-sensitive spending falls in the short run, and physical capital accumulation may slow in the long run

options.text: Private saving disappears in the short run, and the loanable funds market ceases to operate in the long run

options.text: Government borrowing falls in the short run, and the real interest rate necessarily rises in the long run

explanation: The immediate crowding-out effect is a reduction in interest-sensitive private spending caused by higher real interest rates. If the reduction in investment persists, the economy accumulates physical capital more slowly and long-run growth can be lower.

prompt: Government borrowing increases by $180 billion, while the new equilibrium quantity of total loanable funds rises by $70 billion. Assuming the change in total borrowing is divided only between government and private borrowers, what happens to private borrowing?

options.label: A
options.text: It increases by $110 billion

options.label: B
options.text: It increases by $250 billion

options.label: C
options.text: It decreases by $70 billion

options.label: D
options.text: It remains unchanged because total borrowing increased

options.label: E
options.text: It decreases by $110 billion

explanation: Government borrowing rises by more than the total increase in borrowing. The difference, $180 billion - $70 billion = $110 billion, must be a reduction in private borrowing.

prompt: Government borrowing increases by $140 billion and private borrowing falls by $85 billion. What is the change in the equilibrium quantity of total loanable funds?

options.label: A
options.text: It increases by $225 billion

options.label: B
options.text: It increases by $55 billion

options.label: C
options.text: It decreases by $225 billion

options.label: D
options.text: It decreases by $55 billion

options.label: E
options.text: It increases by $85 billion

explanation: The increase in total borrowing equals the government increase minus the displaced private borrowing: $140 billion - $85 billion = $55 billion. This is consistent with crowding out even though total loanable-funds quantity rises.

prompt: The equilibrium quantity of loanable funds increases by $50 billion after a rise in government borrowing, while private borrowing falls by $70 billion. By how much did government borrowing increase?

options.label: A
options.text: $20 billion

options.label: B
options.text: $120 billion

options.label: C
options.text: $170 billion

options.label: D
options.text: $50 billion

options.label: E
options.text: $70 billion

explanation: The total change equals the government borrowing increase plus the change in private borrowing. Thus $50 billion = ΔG borrowing - $70 billion, so government borrowing increased by $120 billion.

prompt: A $100 billion borrowing-financed increase in government purchases raises the real interest rate and crowds out $30 billion of private investment. Which statement is most accurate?

options.label: A
options.text: The crowding-out effect equals $130 billion because public and private spending move in opposite directions

options.label: B
options.text: The government spending increase is only $70 billion because the private investment decline changes government purchases

options.label: C
options.text: The fiscal action is fully crowded out because any decline in private investment eliminates the government spending increase

options.label: D
options.text: The crowding-out effect offsets $30 billion of the direct spending increase, not the entire $100 billion

options.label: E
options.text: The real interest rate must fall after the private investment decline, completely reversing the initial borrowing effect

explanation: Crowding out is measured by the private spending displaced through higher interest rates. A $30 billion investment decline offsets part of the $100 billion direct increase but does not mean the fiscal action is fully neutralized.

prompt: Two policies each increase government purchases by $100 billion. Policy A is financed by $100 billion of new borrowing and crowds out $35 billion of private investment; Policy B is financed by current taxes and causes no additional government borrowing. Considering only crowding out, which policy has the larger direct net spending effect?

options.label: A
options.text: Policy B, because current taxes automatically shift loanable-funds demand right

options.label: B
options.text: Policy A, because crowding out adds $35 billion to the government spending increase, so the real interest rate would move opposite to the usual mechanism

options.label: C
options.text: Policy B, because it does not lose $35 billion of private investment through the borrowing channel

options.label: D
options.text: Both have the same net effect because their government purchases are identical

options.label: E
options.text: Policy A, because the additional borrowing guarantees more private investment

explanation: The two policies have the same direct government-purchase increase, but A triggers the stated $35 billion private-investment offset. Considering only this channel, B retains the larger net increase in spending.

prompt: A borrowing-financed tax cut and a borrowing-financed increase in government purchases each enlarge the budget deficit by the same amount. Which statement about crowding out is most defensible, holding other loanable-funds determinants constant?

options.label: A
options.text: Only the tax cut can cause crowding out because government purchases are part of aggregate demand, because government borrowing would be treated as a source of saving

options.label: B
options.text: Only the spending increase can cause crowding out because tax changes never affect the deficit

options.label: C
options.text: Neither can crowd out private spending because fiscal policy operates outside financial markets

options.label: D
options.text: The tax cut must lower the real interest rate while the spending increase raises it

options.label: E
options.text: Both can create similar upward pressure on the real interest rate because both require additional government borrowing

explanation: For Topic 5.5, the relevant link is the amount of additional government borrowing. If both policies create the same financing need and other market determinants are fixed, both place comparable rightward pressure on loanable-funds demand.

prompt: Government purchases and tax revenues both increase by $60 billion, leaving the budget deficit unchanged. Which conclusion is most appropriate regarding the direct crowding-out channel?

options.label: A
options.text: Private investment must fall by $60 billion because the balanced change exactly displaces it

options.label: B
options.text: Government borrowing must rise by $60 billion because government purchases increased

options.label: C
options.text: The real interest rate must rise because any increase in government purchases causes crowding out, so private financing costs would move in the opposite direction

options.label: D
options.text: Government borrowing must fall by $60 billion because tax revenues increased

options.label: E
options.text: There is no necessary increase in government borrowing from the budget change, so additional crowding out is not implied

explanation: Crowding out is tied to an increase in the government borrowing requirement. If the stated tax and spending changes leave the deficit unchanged, no additional borrowing follows mechanically from that budget change.

prompt: A government increases transfers by $80 billion and raises taxes by $30 billion, financing the remaining $50 billion with borrowing. Which change initiates the Topic 5.5 crowding-out mechanism?

options.label: A
options.text: The $50 billion increase in government borrowing

options.label: B
options.text: The $30 billion tax increase by itself

options.label: C
options.text: The reduction in private saving equal to the tax increase

options.label: D
options.text: The full $80 billion increase in transfer payments regardless of financing

options.label: E
options.text: The increase in government revenue that accompanies the transfer program

explanation: The transfer increase exceeds the tax increase by $50 billion, so the stated financing plan requires $50 billion of additional borrowing. It is that borrowing increase that shifts loanable-funds demand and can crowd out private spending.

prompt: Which chain most accurately connects short-run crowding out to its potential long-run consequence?

options.label: A
options.text: Government borrowing ↓ → real interest rate ↑ → private investment ↓ → physical capital accumulation ↑ → economic growth ↑

options.label: B
options.text: Government borrowing ↑ → real interest rate ↑ → private investment ↓ → physical capital accumulation ↓ → economic growth ↓

options.label: C
options.text: Government borrowing ↑ → real interest rate ↑ → private investment ↑ → physical capital accumulation ↑ → economic growth ↓

options.label: D
options.text: Government borrowing ↑ → real interest rate ↓ → private investment ↓ → physical capital accumulation ↑ → economic growth ↑

options.label: E
options.text: Government borrowing ↑ → real interest rate ↓ → private investment ↑ → physical capital accumulation ↓ → economic growth ↓

explanation: The short-run borrowing channel raises the real interest rate and reduces private investment. Because investment adds to the capital stock, persistent reductions can slow physical capital accumulation and therefore long-run economic growth.

prompt: If crowding out occurs for only a brief period and private investment later returns to its previous path, which statement is most accurate?

options.label: A
options.text: The long-run effect is impossible because short-run private investment never affects physical capital, because the fiscal change would be treated as a supply shift

options.label: B
options.text: The long-run growth effect may be limited because POL-3.C.4 describes lower growth as a potential consequence of reduced capital accumulation

options.label: C
options.text: Economic growth must permanently rise because investment later recovers

options.label: D
options.text: Long-run growth must permanently fall after any amount of short-run crowding out

options.label: E
options.text: The capital stock must permanently fall by the full amount of the government deficit

explanation: The CED deliberately describes the growth effect as potential. A temporary investment shortfall can lower the capital path relative to baseline, but the persistence and later recovery of investment influence how large the long-run effect becomes.

prompt: A larger budget deficit is followed by higher government borrowing and a higher real interest rate, but private investment also rises. Which conclusion is most appropriate?

options.label: A
options.text: Another positive influence offsets the investment decline caused by higher interest rates

options.label: B
options.text: The higher real interest rate proves that crowding out increases private investment

options.label: C
options.text: Rising total investment proves higher interest rates cannot exert crowding-out pressure

options.label: D
options.text: The government borrowing must actually have shifted loanable-funds demand left

options.label: E
options.text: The budget deficit cannot have increased because investment rose

explanation: The higher real interest rate creates downward pressure on interest-sensitive private investment. If investment nevertheless rises, some other determinant must have shifted investment upward by more than the crowding-out effect reduced it.

prompt: A government increases borrowing, and the real interest rate remains at 5 percent. Which evidence would best explain why crowding out is small?

options.label: A
options.text: The budget deficit increased without any change in the demand for loanable funds

options.label: B
options.text: The government borrowing shifted loanable-funds demand left instead of right

options.label: C
options.text: Private investment became more interest sensitive at every real interest rate

options.label: D
options.text: The supply of loanable funds increased enough to accommodate the additional borrowing at roughly the same real interest rate

options.label: E
options.text: The supply of loanable funds decreased by the same amount as government borrowing increased, because government borrowing would be treated as a source of saving

explanation: An increase in the supply of saving can absorb additional borrowing without much increase in the real interest rate. Because private spending is crowded out through higher financing costs, a stable rate implies a smaller interest-rate channel.

prompt: The real interest rate rises and private investment falls, but government borrowing is unchanged. Which conclusion is most accurate?

options.label: A
options.text: The government must have run a larger deficit even though its borrowing is unchanged

options.label: B
options.text: The pattern necessarily proves crowding out because any rate increase that lowers investment qualifies, so private financing costs would move in the opposite direction

options.label: C
options.text: The pattern does not by itself establish crowding out because the defining government-borrowing increase is missing

options.label: D
options.text: Private investment cannot fall when government borrowing is unchanged

options.label: E
options.text: The supply of loanable funds must have shifted right because investment fell

explanation: Crowding out is a particular causal story that starts with increased government borrowing. Higher interest rates and lower investment can arise for other reasons, so those observations alone are insufficient to identify crowding out.

prompt: A recession causes tax revenue to fall and the budget deficit to widen. Assume the government finances the larger deficit through borrowing and all other loanable-funds determinants are unchanged. Which outcome follows from the Topic 5.5 mechanism?

options.label: A
options.text: Government borrowing shifts loanable-funds demand left, lowering the real interest rate and reducing private spending

options.label: B
options.text: Private investment must increase because lower tax revenue raises the budget deficit

options.label: C
options.text: The real interest rate must fall because recessions always eliminate crowding out regardless of financing

options.label: D
options.text: The larger deficit shifts loanable-funds supply right, lowering the real interest rate and increasing private spending, because the fiscal change would be treated as a supply shift

options.label: E
options.text: Government borrowing shifts loanable-funds demand right, raising the real interest rate and reducing interest-sensitive private spending

explanation: Under the stated ceteris paribus assumption, the larger deficit requires more borrowing. The standard Topic 5.5 chain therefore applies even though the deficit originated from weaker tax revenue rather than a discretionary spending increase.

prompt: Which statement most precisely captures the relationship between crowding out and economic growth?

options.label: A
options.text: Crowding out can lower growth by reducing private investment and therefore slowing the accumulation of productive physical capital

options.label: B
options.text: Crowding out lowers growth because government borrowing directly destroys physical capital

options.label: C
options.text: Crowding out raises growth because higher real interest rates always increase private investment

options.label: D
options.text: Crowding out always lowers current real GDP by exactly the amount of government borrowing

options.label: E
options.text: Crowding out affects only current interest rates and has no possible connection to future productive capacity, so the real interest rate would move opposite to the usual mechanism

explanation: The growth effect is indirect: higher government borrowing can raise real interest rates, which can reduce private investment. Sustained lower investment slows the growth of the physical capital stock and can reduce long-run economic growth.

prompt: Suppose a deficit-financed program raises government purchases by $150 billion. Higher real interest rates reduce private investment by $45 billion and interest-sensitive household purchases by $20 billion. Considering only the stated changes, which statement is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: Crowding out offsets $45 billion because household purchases are never interest sensitive

options.label: B
options.text: Crowding out offsets $65 billion of the $150 billion fiscal increase

options.label: C
options.text: Crowding out offsets $150 billion because all government borrowing displaces private spending one-for-one

options.label: D
options.text: Crowding out offsets $215 billion because the government and private changes must be added

options.label: E
options.text: Crowding out adds $65 billion to the fiscal increase because private spending falls

explanation: The CED definition covers interest-sensitive private-sector spending, not investment alone. The private reductions total $45 billion + $20 billion = $65 billion, which partially offsets the $150 billion increase.

prompt: Country A and Country B each increase government borrowing by $100 billion. In A the real interest rate rises by 1 percentage point and private investment falls by $15 billion; in B the rate rises by 3 percentage points and investment falls by $50 billion. Which statement is best supported?

options.label: A
options.text: Country A must have a larger long-run growth effect because its interest-rate increase is smaller, so private financing costs would move in the opposite direction

options.label: B
options.text: Neither experiences crowding out because total loanable-funds quantity is not given

options.label: C
options.text: Both experience identical crowding out because government borrowing rises by the same amount

options.label: D
options.text: Country B experiences more crowding out because the borrowing increase is associated with a larger rate increase and a larger private-investment decline

options.label: E
options.text: Country A experiences more crowding out because its private investment decline is smaller

explanation: Crowding out is identified by the private spending displaced through higher real interest rates. B shows both a larger financing-cost increase and a larger decline in investment, so the observed crowding-out effect is greater.

prompt: A government increases borrowing by $120 billion, but private saving also rises. The equilibrium real interest rate rises only slightly and private investment falls by $10 billion. Which statement is most accurate?

options.label: A
options.text: The real interest rate should have fallen because government borrowing and saving both increase demand, because loanable-funds demand would be assumed to decrease instead

options.label: B
options.text: The small investment decline means government borrowing did not affect loanable-funds demand

options.label: C
options.text: The increase in saving has absorbed part of the borrowing pressure, limiting the amount of crowding out

options.label: D
options.text: The increase in saving has intensified crowding out by shifting loanable-funds supply left

options.label: E
options.text: The amount of crowding out must equal the full $120 billion increase in government borrowing

explanation: The extra saving shifts supply right and tempers the upward movement in the real interest rate. Because the rate rises only slightly, only a small amount of interest-sensitive private investment is displaced.

prompt: A government reduces borrowing by $90 billion, while private saving falls enough that the real interest rate is unchanged. Which statement is most accurate?

options.label: A
options.text: The reduction in borrowing does not necessarily increase private investment because the real interest rate has not fallen

options.label: B
options.text: Private investment must rise by $90 billion because government borrowing fell by that amount

options.label: C
options.text: The unchanged real interest rate proves the demand for loanable funds did not shift

options.label: D
options.text: The unchanged real interest rate proves private saving must have increased rather than decreased

options.label: E
options.text: Private investment must fall because any reduction in government borrowing raises the real interest rate, which would imply less rather than more pressure on private borrowing

explanation: Less government borrowing shifts demand left, but the simultaneous fall in saving shifts supply left and can keep the real interest rate unchanged. Without a lower financing cost, the usual increase in private investment from reduced crowding-out pressure need not occur.

prompt: Which scenario best demonstrates that the size of a budget deficit alone does not determine the size of crowding out?

options.label: A
options.text: Two equal deficit increases produce the same government borrowing increase and the same real interest rate in identical markets, because the fiscal change would be treated as a supply shift

options.label: B
options.text: A government runs a surplus and uses it to reduce outstanding borrowing

options.label: C
options.text: A government runs a deficit and borrows exactly the amount of the deficit in a market with unchanged saving

options.label: D
options.text: Two equal deficit increases produce different real-interest-rate changes because the supply of loanable funds changes differently in the two economies

options.label: E
options.text: A government reduces its deficit and borrowing, causing the real interest rate to fall

explanation: Crowding out depends on the interest-rate response to government borrowing and the resulting private-spending response. If loanable-funds supply conditions differ, the same deficit-financed borrowing increase can produce different rate increases and therefore different amounts of crowding out.
